NOVEMBER 26, 2026 — FROM THE SOCIAL FEED

Day 90 of the Blackout

Ninety days with no power and he's still not panicking. Calendar on the wall says June, Day 90 circled. Lantern lit, candles burning, beans and soup stacked, water boxed up, crank radio ready — and outside the window, the war is still going. A second panda in a helmet is standing watch at the glass.

This is the post that went up on the Pandemik Panda Facebook Page and Instagram @oftheand1 — now filed here on the site where it belongs. No announcement, no countdown, no explanation from anybody in charge. Just day 90, handled the same way as day 1: quiet, stocked, and deadpan.

NOVEMBER 26, 2026 — DEPARTMENT OF WAR, PURSUE RELEASE 08

The Pentagon's UFO Vault Blueprints Are Public

Fox News reported November 26 that the Pentagon's eighth UAP file release includes a 538-page 2009 report from Bigelow Aerospace Advanced Space Studies (BAASS) for the Defense Intelligence Agency, with plans for a 5,000-square-foot underground vault in North Las Vegas — about 20 feet down, 3-foot concrete walls, steel vault door — designed to store "exotic material or tissue." No public record shows the vault was ever built.

THE VERDICT → THEY DREW THE BUNKER FOR THE EVIDENCE. THE PANDA JUST WANTS THE INVENTORY LIST.
NOVEMBER 25, 2026 — SMITHSONIAN MAGAZINE

Earth Has a Second Moon Right Now — It's Six Feet Wide

Smithsonian Magazine reported November 25 that Earth's gravity captured asteroid 2026 QQ8 in April — a roughly six-foot-wide rock confirmed as natural, not space junk, by the International Astronomical Union's Minor Planet Center on October 29. It will keep circling Earth until December or January, then head back out around the sun.

THE VERDICT → A MOON THE SIZE OF A PANDA. IT LEAVES IN DECEMBER. HE'S NOT GETTING ATTACHED.
NOVEMBER 25, 2026 — SMITHSONIAN MAGAZINE / FRONTIERS IN EARTH SCIENCE

A Volcano Exploded Where Explosions Should Be Impossible

Smithsonian Magazine reported November 25 that scientists using the robot submersible Jason/Medea found pyroclastic rocks 20,170 feet down in the Mariana Trench near Challenger Deep — the deepest explosive volcanic eruption ever documented, published November 22 in Frontiers in Earth Science. At that crushing pressure, eruptions are supposed to seep, not explode.

THE VERDICT → 20,000 FEET DOWN AND IT STILL BLEW UP. THE PANDA RESPECTS THE COMMITMENT.

Meet Pandemik Panda

One character, drawn one way, on purpose.

He's not scared.
He read the file.

Pandemik Panda is the mascot of OF THE AND — created by the owner years ago in Photoshop, long before he had a store to put him in. Round head, downcast eyes, deadpan through every disaster: pirates, meteors, bunkers, blacked-out case files. The world ends around him and he's still just standing there, holding his bamboo.

That look never changes, because it's his. Every new design is built from his original artwork, and every shirt pairs him with a piece of the real record — a declassified program, an official report, an event the government itself eventually admitted to. The panda saw it coming because, on paper, it already happened.
